overview.title: A night in the Sahara
overview.p1: A desert camp near Erg Chebbi is the classic way to sleep among the dunes: Berber dinner, music and a sky full of stars after a camel or 4x4 transfer from Merzouga or Hassi Labied.
overview.p2: Camps range from simple shared bivouacs to luxury tents with private bathrooms. Most packages include dinner, breakfast and transport.
overview.p3: Combine with a sunset camel trek for the full Merzouga experience, then wake for sunrise on the ridges.

q1.question: How long do I need at a desert camp?
q1.answer: One night is the classic stay: arrive late afternoon, leave after sunrise. Longer stays are possible at some camps.

q2.question: Is there an entrance fee?
q2.answer: You book a package with the camp (transfer, dinner, night, breakfast). There is no separate public ticket.

q3.question: When is the best time?
q3.answer: Clear evenings year-round; spring and autumn are more comfortable than midsummer heat or midwinter cold.

q4.question: What should I bring?
q4.answer: Warm layer, scarf for sand, power bank, and cash for tips. Toiletries as needed depending on camp standard.

q5.question: How do I get there?
q5.answer: Most camps include camel or 4x4 transfer from Merzouga village or Hassi Labied. Confirm meeting point when you book.
